Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

  6
 To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

Summary:

AB 481 was authored by Assemblymember  David  Chiu (D-San Francisco)  to address the funding,
acquisition,  and use of Military  Equipment  by law enforcement  agencies.  The Assembly  Bill
creates transparency,  oversight,  and accountability  in the acquisition  and use of police  equipment
which  qualifies  as Military  Equipment.  On September  30, 2021, Governor  Newsom  signed AB
481 into law. From AB 481, Government  Code 7071 was adopted which stated that the South Gate
Police  Department  must adopt a Military  Equipment  Policy  and have it approved  by the City
Council.  The South Gate Police Department's  Military  Equipment  Policy  709 was adopted by City
Council on May 10, 2022. Per Governrnent  Code 7072 an annual report  on military  equipment
must be made available to the public.

2025  Military  Equipment  Annual  Report:

The following  are summaries  of the deployments  of military  equipment  during the 2025 calendar
year:

On January  25, 2025,  officers  responded  to strong-arm  robbery  that had just  occurred.  The
suspects, a male and two females, robbed a vendor near the Elizabeth  Bakery  parking  lot and then
drove away in a dark green Ford Explorer.  A SGPD drone was utilized to assist officers  in
canvassing the area for the robbery suspects but was met with negative results.

On January  30, 2025, officers  located  a stolen vehicle  in the area of Southern  Ave and State St.
The driver noticed  the patrol  car following  and abruptly  pulled  into a driveway  on Madison  Ave
and Missouri  Ave.  Three  occupants  fled on foot and officers  gave chase. A SGPD  drone was
deployed to support the search for the suspects which  resulted  in all suspects being apprehended.
A discarded handgun was also recovered.

On February  12, 2025, officers  responded  to the 8600 block of Atlantic  Ave reference  a possible
burglary  in progress  at a warehouse.  Upon  arrival,  a SGPD  drone was deployed  to check the
interior  of building  prior to officers  entering.  Once the initial  check with the drone was conducted,
officers entered the location  and verified  no one was inside.  It was later determined  a burglary
had not occurred.

On February  2, 2025,  officers  responded  to the 8200  block  of Long  Beach  Blvd  reference  a
vandalism  in progress.  Prior  to officers  arrival,  the suspect  le'tt on foot  and entered  the rear yard
of 2456  Cole  Ave  and then  climbed  onto  the roof  of a nearby  residence.  A SGPD  drone  was
deployed  to maintain  visual  of the suspect  who  later  climbed  off  the roof  and was taken  into
custody.

On March  8, 2025,  officers  responded  to the 8900 block  of Elizabeth  Ave  regarding  a report  of
four males  waving  firearms  from  a black  Honda  Accord.  The vehicle  left the scene and was later
located  traveling  south on Garfield  Ave  from  Firestone  Blvd.  Officers  followed  the vehicle  East
on Stewart  and Gray  Rd to Paramount  Blvd.  A high-risk  stop was conducted  on the vehicle.  The
rear passenger  refused  to comply  with  the officer's  commands  and would  at times turn back toward
the officers  or lower  his  arms.  Based  on the totality  of the circumstances,  coupled  with  the
immediate  danger  to the public,  officers  deployed  a less than lethal  40mm  rubber  impact  round,
striking  the suspect  behind  his left leg. The suspect  fell to the ground  and was taken  into custody
by officers  without  further  incident.

On April  6, 2025,  an armed  robbery  occurred  in the area of Wood  Ave  and Atlantic  Ave.  The
suspect  brandished  the grip  of a handgun  in his waistband  and removed  a gold  chain  from  the
victim.  A SGPD  drone was deployed  to search the area. The suspect was located  hiding  in a nearby
residential  garage  and taken  into  custody.  The suspect  was positively  identified  as the robbery
suspect  and placed  under  arrest.

On April  16, 2025, LAJ'D  filed  a 288 PC case involving  a suspect  connected  to CSAM  and sexual
abuse allegations.  During  the investigation,  SGPD narcotics  detectives  assisted  and obtained  drone
footage  of a possible  residence.  Detectives  later executed  a search warrant,  and the suspect  was
booked  for continuous  Sexual  Abuse  of a Child  and possession  of CSAM.

On May 14, 2025, officers  responded  to Tweedy  Blvd  and Alexander  Ave regarding  a male subject
wearing  a tactical  vest armed with  a rifle.  As officers  began setting  up around  the location,  a SGPD
drone  was deployed  to maintain  visual  of the suspect.  Based  on the intelligence  gained  from  the
drone,  officers  were able to tactically  approach  the suspect and detain him without  incident.  It was
later determined  the rifle  was a pellet  gun.

On July  17, 2025,  officers  responded  to the area of the LA  Riverbed  and Firestone  Blvd  after
receiving  reports  of a male carrying  a rifle  in the riverbed.  A SGPD  drone  was deployed  to assist
officers  in canvassing  the area and nearby  encampments.  Officers  checked  several  encampments
and contacted  several  subjects  but did not locate  anyone  in possession  of a rifle.

On September  13, 2025,  SGPD  dispatch  received  a call of suspicious  subjects  possibly  attempting
a "smash  and grab"  at Daniel's  Jewelers  located  at Azalea  Center.  The R/P advised  that a group  of
subjects  wearing  black hoodies  and masks with bags and bats attempted  to enterthe  business  which
was still  closed.  The subjects  were last seen walking  southbound  Burke  Ave.  A SGPD  drone  was
deployed  to assist officers  canvassing  the area. Officers  located  four subjects  matching  the suspect
description  at South  Gate Park Sports  Center.  When  officers  attempted  to detain  the subjects,  one
of the subjects  discarded  a loaded  semi-auto  handgun.  During  the investigation,  officers  found  the

709.1  PURPOSE  AND  SCOPE

 The  purpose  of this  policy  is to provide  guidelines  for the  approval,  acquisition,  and  reporting
 requirements  of military  equipment  (Government  Code  § 7070;  Government  Code  § 7071;
 Government  Code  § 7072).

  709.1.1  DEFINITIONS

 Definitions  related  to this policy  include  (Government  Code  § 7070):

 Governing  body  - The South  Gate  City Council.

709.2  POLICY

 It is the policy of the South Gate Police Department  that members  of this department  comply  with
 the provisions  of Government  Code § 7071 with respect  to military  equipment.

709.3  MILITARY  EQUIPMENT  COORDINATOR

 The Chief of Police should designate  a member  of this department  to act as the military  equipment
 coordinator.  The responsibilities  ofthe  military equipment  coordinator  include but are not limited to:

  (a)  Acting as liaison to the governing  body for matters  related  to the requirements  of this
  policy.

  (b)  Identifying department  equipment  that qualifies as military equipment in the current
  possession  of the Department,  or the equipment the South Gate Police Department
  intends to acquire that requires approval by the South Gate City Council.

  (c)  Conducting  an inventory  of all military  equipment  at least annually.

  (d)  Collaborating  with any allied agency that  may use military equipment  within  the
  jurisdiction  of South Gate Police Department  (Government  Code § 7071).

  (e)  Preparing  for, scheduling,  and  coordinating  the  annual  community  engagement
  meeting to include:

  1.  Publicizing  the details  of the meeting.

  2.  Preparing for public questions  regarding  the department's  funding,  acquisition,
  and use of equipment.

  (f)  Preparing the annual military equipment  report for submission  to the Chief of Police
  and ensuring that the report is made available on the department  website (Government
  Code § 7072).

  (g)  Establishingtheprocedureforapersontoregisteracomplaintorconcern,orhowthat
  person may submit a question about the use of a type of military  equipment,  and how
  the Department will respond in a timely manner.

  709.1  PURPOSE  AND SCOPE
  The purpose  of this policy is to provide  guidelines  for the approval,  acquisition,  and reporting
  requirements  of military  equipment  (Government  Code  § 7070;  Government  Code  § 7071;
  Government  Code § 7072). With the adoption ofthis  policy by the South Gate City Council,  it has
  been determined  that no other reasonable  altemative  exists that can achieve  same objective  of
  officer and civilian safety;  It is most cost-effective  method to achieve  officer and civilian safety;
  and it is will safe guard the public's welfare,  civil rights, safety and civil liberties.

  709.1.1  DEFINITIONS
  Definitions  along with descriptions  contained  within this policy are consistent  with those stated in
  Government  Code § 7070.

  709.2  POLICY
  It is the policy of the South Gate Police Department  that members  of this department  comply with
  the provisions  of Government  Code § 7071 with respect to military equipment.

  709.3  MILITARYEQUIPMENTCOORDINATOR
  The Chief of Policewill  designate  a member  of this department  to act as the military equipment
  coordinator.  The responsibilities  ofthe military equipment  coordinatorinclude  but are not limited to:

  (a)  Acting as liaison to the governing  body for matters related to the requirements  of this
  policy.

  (b)  Identifying department equipment that qualifies as military equipment in the current
  possession of the Department, or the equipment the Department intends to acquire
  that requires approval by the South Gate City Council.

  (c)  Conducting  an inventory  of all military equipment  at least annually.

  (d)  Collaborating  with any allied agency that may use military equipment within  the
  jurisdiction of South Gate Police Department (Government Code § 707'l ).

  (e)  Preparing for, scheduling,  and  coordinating  the  annual  community  engagement
  meeting to include:

  1.  Publicizing  the details of the meeting.

  2.  Preparing for public questions  regarding  the department's  funding,  acquisition,
  and use of equipment.

  (f)  Preparing the annual military equipment report for submission to the Chief of Police
  and ensuring thatthe report is made available on the departmentwebsite (Government
  Code § 7072).

  (g)  Establishing the procedure for a person to register a complaint or concem, or how that
  person may submit a question about the use of a type of military equipment, and how

g  the Department will respond in a timely manner.

ANALYSIS:  On  October  25,  2022,  the  City  Council  adopted  Ordinance  No.  2022-09-CC
granting  Torrance  Pipeline  Company,  LLC  (TPC)  a Franchise  Agreement  to  maintain  and
operate  Pipeline  No.  M-145.  The pipeline  consists  of approximately  1.7 miles  (8,960  feet)  of
active  12-inch-diameter  pipe  and is the only  active  TPC-owned  line within  the City.  Ordinance
No.  2022-09-CC  expires  on September  13,  2026.  The  proposed  Franchise  Agreement  would
renew  the authorization  for a 5-year  term  beginning  September  13, 2026, through  September  13,
2031.  The  Franchise  Agreement  currently  includes  a provision  stating  that  the  term  will
automatically  renew  for  an additional  five  (5) years  unless  the City  provides  written  notice  of
termination  at least sixty  (60) days prior  to the expiration  date.

The proposed  Franchise  Agreement  is substantially  the same as the current  agreement,  except  for
the effective  period,  term,  and fees. Key provisions  include:

  @  A 5-year  term from  September  13, 2026,  through  September  13, 2031,  with  an automatic
  5-year  renewal  unless  the City  provides  written  notice  of termination  at least sixty  (60)
  days prior  to the expiration  date. Terms  and conditions  consistent  with  California  Public
  Utilities  Code Section  6201 and the proposed  Ordinance.

  Pipeline  maintenance  in compliance  with  all applicable  city,  county,  state,  and federal
  laws,  regulations,  and requirements.  Requires  pipeline  pressure  testing  at a frequency
  consistent  with  State and Federal  requirements  as a preventive  leak detection  and safety
  measure.

  *  Requires  that any damage  to any public  property  caused  shall  be promptly  repaired  by
  Franchisee  at its sole cost and expense.

  *  Liability  insurance,  bonding,  and indemnification  requirements.

  Franchise  payments  and operating  requirements  governing  TPC's  use of the public  right-
  of-way.

  @  A  comprel'iensive  emergency  response  plan  n'ieeting  federal  and  state  requirements,
  including  24-hour  notification  and  emergency  response  services  (traffic  control,
  excavation,  repair,  and necessary  supplies/services)  within  two  (2) hours  of notice,  and
  restoration  of public  streets,  alleys,  or parkways  within  seventy-two  (72) hours.

  2  54
 The Pipeline  is located  within  500 feet of the East Los Angeles  Community  College  expansion
project,  Southeast  High  School,  and  Simon  Rodia  Continuation  School.  The  Franchise
Agreement  requires  TPC  to operate  the Pipeline  in accordance  with  Government  Code  Section
51010,  under  which  the  California  State  Fire  Marshal  has  exclusive  safety  regulatory  and
enforcement  authority  over  hazardous  liquid  pipelines.  The  State Fire Marshal  is authorized  to
implement  the federal  Hazardous  Liquid  Pipeline  Safety  Act  (49 U.S.C.  Sec. 2001  et seq.) and
related  federal  pipeline  safety  regulations  as needed to maintain  annual  federal  certification.

Accordingly,  the Pipeline  must  be used,  operated,  repaired,  and modified  in compliance  with
safety  regulations  established  by the California  State Fire  Marshal  and, as applicable,  the fire
authority  having  jurisdiction,  consistent  with  Chapter  13.14  (Special  Provisions  for  Oil
Pipelines),  Division  1 (Oil,  Gas and Water  Pipelines),  Title  13 (Francises)  of the South  Gate
Municipal  Code.  The  State Fire  Marshal  is also required  to conduct  annual  inspections  of the
Pipeline  to veri:[y  compliance,  and TPC must  submit  certified  test results  pursuant  to the Pipeline
Safety  Act of 1981.

BACKGROUND:  On April  14, 2026,  the City  Council  adopted  Resolution  No.  2026-13-CC
declaring  the  City's  intention  to  grant  a franchise  to  Torrance  Pipeline  Company,  LLC,  a
Delaware  limited  liability  company,  for the continued  operation  of an existing  oil transmission
pipeline  within  the City.  Introduction  of the proposed  Ordinance  is the second  of three  required
City  Council  actions  necessary  to grant the Franchise  Agreement.

Pipeline  No.  M-145  transports  refined  oil products  from  the Torrance  Refinery  to the Vernon
Terminal  through  the City  of South  Gate. Within  the City,  the pipeline  is located  beneath  Santa
Fe Avenue  from  Independence  Avenue  to Southern  Avenue,  Southern  Avenue  from  Santa  Fe
Avenue  to Alameda  Street,  and Alameda  Street  from  Southern  Avenue  to Seminole  Avenue,
forming  one continuous  pipeline  alignment.

The proposed  schedule  for issuance  of the Franchise  Agreement  is as follows:

  1.  April  14,  2026  - The  City  Council  adopted  Resolution  No.  2026-13-CC  declaring  the
  City's  intention  to grant a franchise  agreement  to TPC.

  2.  May  12, 2026 - The City  Council  conducted  the required  public  hearing  and introduced
  Ordinance  No.  granting  the franchise  to TPC.

  3.  May  26, 2026 - City  Council  considered  the ordinance  for adoption;  however,  based  on
  public  comments  and  Council  direction,  the  item  was  continued  to allow  for  further
  review  and additional  information  before  final  action.

  4.  July  14, 2026 - City  Council  will  consider  adopting  the Ordinance  granting  the franchise
  to TPC,  along  with  any updated  terms  and supporting  information  included  in the staff
  report.

TPC  has requested  renewal  of the  franchise  for  Pipeline  No.  M-145  (Ordinance  No.  2329).
Approval  is recommended  for the following  reasons:

  3  55

SECTION  9:  Emergency  Procedures.

  A)  Grantee  shall  develop  and maintain  an emergency  response  plan,  satisfactory  to the City
  Engineer,  which  covers  all franchise  operations  within  the City.  The initial  draft  of that
  emergency  response  plan shall be delivered  to the City Engineer  not later than the Effective

  arrangements  capable  of providing  emergency  response  services,  including  but not limited
  to traffic  control,  street excavation,  pipeline  repair,  and supplies  and services  as necessary,
  within  two (2) hours of notification  of any problem,  and such other information  as the City
  Engineer  shall  reasonably  require.  Repairs  to a public  street,  alley  or parkway  shall  be
  completed  within  seventy-two  (72) hours unless otherwise  authorized  by the City Engineer.
  The City  Engineer  shall be notified  ten (10) days in advance  of any proposed  change  in
  such arrangements.

  products  thereof  into  the public  right-of-way,  Grantee,  and any other  person  using  or
  controlling  the  Pipeline  or Appurtenance,  shall  immediately  notify  the  City's  Police
  Department  and  Public  Works  Department  and  shall  implement  precautionary  safety
  measures  including  traffic  control,  system  shutdown,  valve  closures,  and  public
  notification.  In the event of an emergency  which  threatens  life, health,  safety  or property,
  and where  it is not possible  to obtain  an excavation  permit  prior  to commencement  of the
  work,  the Grantee  may commence  such work;  provided,  however,  that within  seventy-two
  (72) hours thereafter  Grantee  shall make application  to the City Engineer  for an excavation
  permit  in accordance  with  the procedures  specified  herein.  The City Engineer  may impose
  conditions  upon  the issuance  of the excavation  permit,  and all work  shall  be subject  to
  inspection.  Adequate  traffic  safety  barriers  shall  be maintained  at all times,  and any
  damaged  portion  of the Street shall be restored  to its original  condition.

  compliance with the NPDES Permit Program. These services include regulatory compliance
  suppejt't, permit reporting, program administration, and implementation oversight related to the
  City's Watershed Management Plan,

  The current contract term expired on June 30, 2026, and may be extended for one additional year
  in accordance with the contract provisions. Staff is recommending approvaI of the final one-year
  contract extension in an amount not to exceed $111,643.

  The NPDES Program is Mghly techriical and involves complex regulatory requirements, ongoing
  reporting obligations, and strict compliance standards. Failure to comply withpermittequirements

JHA has provided  specialized  support  to the City  and has consistently  performed  in a professional

continued  expert  support  for tis  critical  regulatory  program.

BACKGROUND:  The City  maintains  an extensive  storm  drain  infrastructure  system  consisting
of catch  basins,  pipelines,  and drainage  facilities  designed  to capture  and convey  stormwater
runoff  throughout  the City.  This  system  collects  stormwater  from  streets, parking  lots, and other
developed  areas and discharges  it into regional  waterways,  including  the Los Angeles  River,  Rio
Hondo  Channel,  and Compton  Creek.  Because  stormwater  runoff  can carry  pollutants  such as
trash, sediment,  oil, and other contaminants,  proper  management  of the City's  stormwater  system
is critical  to protecting  water  quality  and public  health.

The  State of California  regulates  stormwater  quality  through  the National  Pollutant  Discharge
Elimination  System  (NPDES)  Permit  Program,  which  is designed  to prevent  pollutants  from
entering  local  waterways.  Under  this  program,  the City  is required  to manage,  monitor,  and
regulate  stormwater  discharges  to  ensure  compliance  with  State  and  federal  water  quality
regulations.

The  NPDES  Program  is  highly  technical  and  complex,  involving  extensive  regulatory
requirements,  annual  reporting,  compliance  monitoring,  and  implementation  of  a Watershed
Management  Plan  with  an estimated  cost  exceeding  $61  million  through  2028.  Due  to the
complexity  and specialized  nature  of the program,  the Department  of Public  Works  relies  on JHA
to provide  expert  consulting  services.  Their  specialized  knowledge  helps ensure the City  remains
in compliance  with  permit  requirements  and avoids  potential  regulatory  violations,  fines,  and
penalties.

On August  9, 2022,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No.  2022-63-CC  with  JHA  for a three-
year term in the amount  of $334,155 to provide  stormwater  management  services  for Fiscal  Years
2022/23,  2023/24,  and 2024/25.  The contract  included  provisions  allowing  forup  to two additional
one-year  extensions.

On August  12, 2025,  the City  Council  approved  Amendment  No.  I to Contract  No. 2022-63-CC
in the amount  of $111,643,  to exercise  the first one-year  extension  ofthe  contract  to June 30, 2026.
ArnendmentNo.  2 to ContractNo.  2022-63-CC  represents  the second and final  one-year  extension
permitted  under  the contract.

Based on John L. Hunter  and Associates'  satisfactory  performance,  specialized  expertise,  and the
continued  need for support  in managing  the City's  complex  NPDES  compliance  requirements,
staff recommend  approval  of Amendment  No. 2 to extend  the contract  for one additional  year.

John L. Hunter and Associates, Inc. (JLHA) is an environmental  consulting  corporation  founded  in

1985. We specialize in assisting municipalities implement water quality and conservation
programs. These programs include NPDES, stormwater  pollution prevention, watershed
management,  sewer overflow  prevention,  water conservation,  and recycling.  Services include
program administratron,  planning,  reporting,  and funding,  as well as inspections,  engineering,
monitoring,  and public education.

  *  Assisting  with  the  implementation  of the  Statewide  Trash  Provisions  for  22 local

  PURPOSF,:  The proposed  Agreement  will  provide  financial  assistance  to the South  Gate Chamber  of
  Cornrnerce  ("Chamber")  to advertise  and ptomote  the residential,  commercial,  and industrial  advantages
  of the City,  and the benefits  of living  in or locating  business  or industry  within  the City  of South Gate
  during  Fiscal Year 2026/27.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  the South  Gate Chamber  of Commerce  for promotion  of
  community  activities  in Fiscal  Year 2026/27  in the amount not to exceed $25,000;  and
  b.  AuthorizingtheMayortoexecutetheAgreementinafotmacceptabletotheCityAttorney,

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  If approved,  funds  in the amount  of $25,000  will  be included  in the Fiscal  Year
  2026/27  Budget  in Account  Number  100-120-12-6308  (General  Fund - City  Manager  Administration  -
  Civic  Engagement).

  ANALYSIS:  The approval  ofthe  proposed  Agteement  will  enable the Chamber  to continue  advertising
  and promotin;g  activities  that support  the goals of encouraging  economic  development  and workforce
  development,  as well as improving  communications  and civic  engagement  in the City of South Gate.

  BACKGROUND:  Over the past several years, the City has contracted  on ayearly  basis withthe
  Chamber  to undertake  business promotion  activities.  Currently,  the Chamber  is requesting  funding  from
  the City in an amount  not to exceed $25,000  for Fiscal Year 2026/27  to continue  providing  services to
  the South Gate residents  and business community.  Due to budget  constraints,  this funding  request is for
  half the amount  the City provided  in previous  fiscal years, The payment  schedule  shall consist  of two
  installtnents  during  the fiscal year.  The first installment  will  require  a Financial  Statement,  and the
  second installment  will  request the Petormance  Summary  prior to receiving  payment.

 Continued  Activities  and Services
Using  the requested  funding,  the Chamber  will  continue  to disseminate  information  to the public  about
the benefits  of locating  a business  in the City;  serve as an informational  bureau;  maintain  an office
within  the City  which  is accessible  to the public;  publicize  City-sponsored  activities  and functions;
advertise  and promote  the commercial  expansion  and development  of the City;  and work  with  the City,
County,  and other public  and private  agencies  to obtain  appropriate  information  and services  for
prospective  businesses.  Furthermore,  the Agreement  includes  partnering  with  civic  groups  to
collaboratively  host a "speaker  series"  event each year for local  businesses  and conducting  ribbon-
cutting  ceremonies  for new South  Gate businesses.

The Chamber  will  also continue  to host the Mayor's  State of the City  Address,  the Career  Workforce
Development  Expo,  and the Southeast  Los Angeles  County  Business  Expo,  to name  a few.  The City  is
unable to support  the Children's  Christmas  Lane Parade this year due to the $90,000  internal  cost in Public
Works  and Police  Department  services  to close the streets and maintain  security.

The proposed  Agreement  will  continue  to include  the same performance  measurement  as the previous
agreement,  whereby  the Chamber  will  work  to increase  its membership  by at least 15% each year.

Tax-Exempt  Status
The tax-exempt  status  of the Chamber  has been confirmed  by the Franchise  Tax Board  and California
Secretary of State.
